source.title: Incomplete suppression of distractor-related activity in the frontal eye field results in curved saccades

confidence_rationale: Causal microstimulation plus recording, in primate, showing suppression is a graded competitive process WITHIN the selection map whose residue leaks into behaviour -- which cuts against the 'separate suppression module' reading of Q-082 while confirming suppression is genuinely pre-behavioural. Mixed because it supports the pre-selection timing but weakens the separable-substrate framing.
failure_signatures: Suppression is INCOMPLETE and time-varying at the moment of commitment, and the residual distractor activity biases the executed action continuously rather than being cleanly gated out -- a binary pre-selection filter does not reproduce curved trajectories.

Distractor-coding activity and target-coding activity live in the SAME map; suppression is expressed as relative activity within the selection substrate, so an architecture that adds a separate suppression module may double-count a function the priority competition already performs.
Selection can be committed BEFORE competition resolves -- the bottleneck does not wait, which means a top-k boundary can emit a contaminated selection rather than failing visibly.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Saccades curving toward a distractor are accompanied by increased perisaccadic activity in frontal eye field neurons coding the distractor location and saccades curving away by decreased activity, while target-coding activity is unchanged; subthreshold microstimulation mimicking the recorded distractor activity causally induced curvature toward the stimulated location, indicating curvature results from incomplete suppression of distractor-related activity during target selection.
mapping.ree_translation: REE reads this as the counterweight to Mysore & Knudsen within the same question. Suppression here is not a separate gate upstream of a selection map -- it is the graded competitive dynamics OF the map, and its incompleteness at commitment time leaks directly into the executed action. On this reading, precision-weighted cue routing plus the MECH-254 top-k bottleneck may already instantiate the relevant function, and the correct REE question becomes whether the bottleneck can commit before competition resolves rather than whether a suppression module is missing.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The behavioural readout is saccade trajectory curvature, a continuous motor variable with no REE analogue -- REE's committed actions are discrete, so the specific 'incomplete suppression leaks into the trajectory' signature cannot manifest. The analogous REE signature would be contamination of a committed discrete selection, which this paper does not measure and which may have different dynamics. Also FEF is cortical oculomotor, one node in a larger selection network including SC.
mapping.source_context: Macaque (Macaca mulatta), frontal eye field single-unit recording during visual search with distractors, plus subthreshold microstimulation causal manipulation.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality high for its era and design -- the microstimulation arm converts a correlation into a causal claim, which is what makes it usable. Mapping fidelity limited by the continuous-trajectory readout having no discrete-action counterpart in REE.
